primarySource.title: CCI Notes 11/10 — Encapsulation
primarySource.personalReading: Full CCI page reread, including film characteristics, exclusions, preparation, sealing, envelope procedure, endnotes and remaining page sections.

routes.predicate: The CCI endnote exception to the corner-gap instruction when sealing polyester envelopes.
routes.prompt: CCI advises leaving a small gap at the corners of a tape-sealed polyester envelope so air can escape. Which statement correctly identifies when its instructions say the gap is unnecessary?

answers.text: A corner gap is required for every way of sealing polyester film.
answers.note: CCI requires a small corner gap in its tape procedure, but Endnote 5 makes a machine-sealing exception.
answers.primaryGround: CCI lines 76 and Endnote 5 line 248 distinguish tape setup from machine-sealed envelopes.

answers.text: A corner gap is unnecessary with double-sided tape because smoothing expels the air.
answers.note: CCI describes smoothing tape to adhere the film and squeeze out air, but the endnote still specifies the no-gap exception only for machine sealing.
answers.primaryGround: The taping procedure says leave a small gap at corners to avoid trapped air and puckering; the smoothing step is separate.

answers.text: Ultrasonic or heat-sealed envelopes need a corner gap so air can escape.
answers.note: Endnote 5 states the opposite: the machine expels air automatically, so no gap is required.
answers.primaryGround: CCI Endnote 5 directly says no gap is required for ultrasonic or heat-sealing machines because air is expelled automatically.

answers.text: No corner gap is required with ultrasonic or heat-sealing machines; air is expelled automatically.
answers.note: This is CCI Endnote 5’s explicit exception. The distinction applies to those machines, not to the double-sided-tape instructions.
answers.primaryGround: CCI Endnote 5 directly says no gap is required for ultrasonic or heat-sealing machines because air is expelled automatically.

routes.whyHard: Requires a precise preservation-procedure exception located in an endnote, and distinguishing machine sealing from the ordinary tape procedure. This is source-specific conservation knowledge, not a general property of envelopes.
routes.reviewQuestion: Reviewer should confirm that the options are sufficiently plausible and the endnote exception merits frozen HARD.

routes.predicate: CCI’s stated film-thickness examples by artifact class.
routes.prompt: Which pairing matches CCI’s typical polyester-film thickness guidance for paper artifacts?

answers.text: 7 mil is standard for most documents; 3 mil is more usual for heavier large maps.
answers.note: CCI gives the reverse pairing: 3 mil is standard for most documents/manuscripts, while 7 mil is more usual for heavier items such as large maps.
answers.primaryGround: CCI lines 35–36 pair 3 mil with most documents/manuscripts and 7 mil with heavier items such as large maps.

answers.text: 3 mil is standard for documents and manuscripts; the same thickness is usual for heavier large maps.
answers.note: CCI ties the chosen thickness to artifact size and gives 7 mil as more usual for heavier objects such as large maps.
answers.primaryGround: The source says film thickness largely depends on artifact size and names a thicker 7 mil example for heavier maps.

answers.text: 3 mil is more usual for heavier large maps; 7 mil is standard for most documents.
answers.note: CCI gives the reverse pairing: standard 3 mil for most documents/manuscripts and the thicker 7 mil for heavier large maps.
answers.primaryGround: CCI lines 35–36 directly contrast the two thicknesses and artifact classes.

answers.text: 3 mil is standard for most documents and manuscripts; 7 mil is more usual for heavier items such as large maps.
answers.note: CCI provides this typical pairing and gives the corresponding film thicknesses as 0.003 and 0.007 inches.
answers.primaryGround: CCI lines 35–36 state both the usual classes and inch equivalents; the added note fact gives the conversions.

routes.whyHard: Requires specialist recall of archival polyester film specifications and the nuanced size/weight distinction between ordinary papers and large, heavy artifacts; no ordinary-adult convention supplies the 3/7 mil pairing.
routes.reviewQuestion: Reviewer should check whether exact technical specification recall is sufficient for HARD under project rubric.

limitations: No catalog edits, no candidate/sourceproof packet, no application, no independent cycle spent. Each answer note is tied to exact CCI text; distractor notes state the source-backed correction.
